as_told.title: Townsend Brown takes material from the 1958 Hartford crash

tellings.quote: The year is 1960. Residents near Hartford, Connecticut, see a greenish fireball in the sky. It makes a loud noise as it comes crashing down to Earth. An observer hears the crash and follows it, going outside to find a shed on fire. Metal debris is found in the vicinity.
tellings.difference: Dates the crash to 1960 rather than 1958, adds the green fireball and burning shed, and cites a Smithsonian archive file.
tellings.link_reason: The same Hartford, Connecticut crash, documented by Swords, with Brown taking the material from Harvard.

as_told.title: Robert Lusser, Townsend Brown and green fireball material

plain: Michels tells how residents near Hartford, Connecticut, saw a greenish fireball crash with a loud noise, how a man who followed the sound found a shed on fire, and how metal debris was picked up nearby. The material went first to the astronomers Fred Whipple and J. Allen Hynek at Moonwatch, a Harvard program for observing and tracking the world's first satellites. An officer named Robert Friend at Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, also wanted the samples, but the scientist Thomas Townsend Brown simply "walks in to Harvard, flashes his credentials, and takes the material." Michels dates the crash to 1958 in one telling and to 1960 in others, and credits the researcher Michael Swords and a file in the Smithsonian archive as his sources.
